questions.title: Photoelectric experiment and uncertainty
questions.stem: Students set up the apparatus shown to study the photoelectric effect; in particular, the relationship between the frequency and intensity of incoming light and the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons. Assume that all the filters give light of the same intensity. With one filter in place and the same light source, the students slowly increase the voltage from zero and plot the current as a function of the voltage.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the current drops to zero at point X.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Determine the value of Planck's constant, h, that the students would have obtained from this graph. Give your answer in eV s.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Describe how you would use uncertainty bars to decide whether a straight line of best fit is justified.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ejected photoelectrons cross the phototube provided their kinetic energy exceeds the potential energy of the reversed DC voltage. As that voltage is increased, fewer photoelectrons have sufficient kinetic energy, until even the most energetic are stopped — point X.

parts.label: c
parts.text: 4.8 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV s. The gradient of the graph gives h.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Fit uncertainty bars of the indicated size to all points, then check whether a straight line of best fit passes through the extent of every bar.
